Genie R. Fortu Punong Barangay Gentlemen/Ladies: This has reference to the undated letter of Mr. Artemio L Hernandez requesting for legal opinion regarding the thirty-peso (PhP30.OO) per household monthly fee being collected by the Sangguniang Barangay intended to defray garbage collection expenses by virtue of Barangay Ordinance No. 02, Series of 2012, entitled "Ordinansa ng Sangguniaqv Barangay ng Lumangbayan, Lungsod ng Calapan, Silangang Mindoro na Nagtatakda sa Lahat ng Tahanan ng Barangay Lumangbayan, Lungsod ng Calapan na Mag-Ambag ng Piso (Pl.(M) Kada Araw Upang Mapanatili ang Kalinisan at Kaayusan ng Barangay at Upang Maisaayos ang Problema sa Basura ". A careful review of the aforesaid barangay ordinance would readily reveal its laudable and honest intention of maintaining cleanliness and health in your locality. Garbage collection is one of the primary governmental functions delegated to barang9Y units for the promotion of the general welfare. Contrary to the assertion of Mr. Hernandez in his letter, we find nothing Sections 11 and 12 of the "Ecological Solid Waste Management Act" (R.A. 9003) which mandates that "Barangay Council through an ordinance shall establish an Ecological Solid Waste Management Committee and must allocate barangay funds for the said program and must be approved by the Sangguniang Barangay. " Be that as it may, there is nothing to prevent your Sangguniang Barangay from allocating barangay funds or to generate and apply resources, to include levying of fees, taxes and other charges, for the accomplishment of its governmental functions, pursuant to Sections 18 and 129 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991". However, may we remind you that laudable and honest intentions, as well as the performance of certain governmental functions, are not grounds to exempt your Sangguniang Barangay from complying with specific legal and Statutory requisites. It is the Department's considered opinion that the barangay ordinance in question is lewlly infirm, based on the following reasons: First, a Special Report from our Field Office disclosed that Barangay Ordinance No. 02, Series of 2012, did not comply with Section 57 of the Local Government Code of 1991, considering that the said "ordinance (Ord. No. 2S 2012) was not endorsed to the Sangguniang Panlungsod for review. " It must be noted that the provision of the said Section 57 is mandatory in nature and that non-compliance therewith renders the subject barangay ordinance legally defective.

Thus, Section 57 of the Local Government Code provides: "Section 5Z Review of Baran a Ordinan Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan. b the San nian (a) Within ten IO da after its enactment the san unian ra a shall co ies of all to th panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned for review as to whether the ordinance is consistent with law and city or municipal ordinances. (b) Ifthe sangguniang panlungsod or sanuuniang bayan, as the case may be, fails to take action on barangay ordinances within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, the same shall be deemed approved. (c) Ifthe sarwuniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan, as the case may be, finds the barangay ordinances inconsistent with law or city or municipal ordinances, the sanggunian concerned shall, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, return the same with its comments and recommendations to the sangguniang barangay concerned for adjustment, amendment, or modification; in which case, the effectivity of the barangay ordinance is suspended until such time as the revision called for is effected. " (Italics and underscoring supplied) Second, there is no showing that your Sangguniang Barangay likewise with the mandatory provision of Section 59 of the said Local Government Code of 1991 regarding the posting requirements applicable to the disputed barangay ordinance. Section 59 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides: "Section 59. Effectivity of Ordinances or Resolutions. - (a) Unless otherwise stated in the ordinance or the resolution approving the local development plan and public investment program, the same shall take effect after ten (IO) days from the date a copy thereof' is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the provincial capitol or city, municipal, or barangay hall, as the case may and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. posting of an ordinance resolution in the bulletin board at the entrance of the provincial capitol and the city, municipal, or barangay hall in at least two (2) conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned not later than five (5) da after approval thereof.

C) The text of the ordinance or resolution shall be disseminated and posted in Filipino or English and in the Igpguage understood by the majority of the people in the local government unit concerned, and the secretary to the sanggunian shall record such fact in a book kept for the statin the dates ofa rovaland tin (c) The gist of all ordinances with penal sanctions shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the province where the local legislative body concerned belongs. In the absence of any newspaper of general circulation within the province, posting of such ordinances shall be made in all municipalities and cities of the province where the sanggunian of origin is situated. (d) In the case of highly urbanized and independent component cities, the main features of the ordinance or resolution duly enacted or adopted shall, in addition to being posted, be published once in a local newspaper of general circulation within the city: Provided, That in the absence thereof the ordinance or resolution shall be published in any newspaper of general circulation. " (Italics and underscoring supplied) Posting is specially required as a requirement of due process considering that Barangay Ordinance No. 02 contemplates a penal provision under "SEKSYON III" thereof, in compliance with the doctrine laid down in the case of Berdin, et al. vs. Mascarifias, et al., G.R. No. 135928, 06 July 2007. Third, appropriate checks and balances for the safety and security of public funds must be established as regards the funds collected for garbage disposal. It must be stressed that the funds collected by virtue of the barangay ordinance concerned is in the nature of public funds. As such, the same may not be deposited under a private account in RCBC Savings Bank (Account No. 1154-00299-2), and disbursed as if it is a private fund. Incidentally, nothing in the same barangay ordinance authorized the opening ot an account by any person with the said RCBC Savings bank in behalf of the barangay. This in itself is a violation of the law for being an unauthorized or an ultra vires act. In addition to the above, proper receipts, for accounting and audit purposes, must be issued by the concerned barangay council for each household paying the mandated monetary exaction. Clearly, without proper compliance with the foregoing legal requirements and observations, the assailed barangay ordinance cannot be given effect and that us present implementation becomes illegal. This is regardless of the good and honest intentions behind the said barangay measure. "Under the principle Chat ours is a government of

laws and not of men. every official must act by and within the authority ofa valid law and cannotiustify the lack of it on thepretext alone of gocxl intentions. 1 " Having said the foregoing, you are hereby advised to adopt corrective action/s thereon. Your continued implementation of an ordinance which violates the provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 constitutes a ground for possible administrative charges against you pursuant to Section 60 of the aforesaid law or Section 19 of Republic Act No. 6770, otherwise known as the Ombudsman Act of 1989, subject to the rule on primary jurisdiction. Thank you. I.LLS:25/11 Copy furnished: ENGR. JAMES F. FADRILAN Officer-in-Charge DILG-Region IV-B (MIMAROPA) 10TH Fir.. BEN-LOR Bldg. Brgy. Paligsahan, 1184-A Quezon Ave., Quezon City MR. ARTEMIO L.
